title: Remove Duplicates
story: The registration desk typed some ticket numbers twice.
goal: Read numbers separated by commas. Print the sorted list of unique numbers, like [1, 2, 3].
starter:
line = input()
# unique, sorted, as a list of ints
hints: Split on commas, turn each piece into an int, then use set() to drop duplicates.
sorted(set(numbers)) gives a sorted list of the unique values.

line = input()
numbers = [int(x) for x in line.split(",")]
print(sorted(set(numbers)))
socratic: Why convert to int before sorting?
Compare your output with the goal. What differs?
explain: In one sentence: what is the key idea in “Remove Duplicates”?
solution:
line = input()
numbers = [int(x) for x in line.split(",")]
print(sorted(set(numbers)))
alt:
line = input()
seen = []
for x in line.split(","):
    n = int(x)
    if n not in seen:
        seen.append(n)
seen.sort()
print(seen)
